correctness.rationale: The barycentric variance identity gives r_q^2=s^2(q-1)/(2q) and forces a unique centroid when a ball contains q vertices. Pigeonhole forces a k-vertex ball in any two-ball cover, hence radius >=r_k. The hyperplane sum_A lambda_i=1/2 cuts the entire simplex into two convex cells whose vertices are selected original vertices and cross-edge midpoints. Those midpoints have squared distance s^2/4 to both complementary face centroids, no larger than r_k^2 and r_l^2, so convexity covers the entire body rather than only its vertices. In odd dimensions both balls must contain disjoint k-vertex groups at exact radius and their centers are unique; in even dimensions the radius slack r_k-r_(k-1)>0 gives a ball of second-center perturbations. Valid for all integer d>=3; no total optimizer classification for even d.
